sentences.text: Leptocleidus was a small plesiosaur that reached a maximum length of 3 meters.
This animal possessed a triangular skull with a crest extending from the nose tip to the nasal region.
The species L. superstes was the smallest, measuring approximately 1.5 meters in length.
Researchers suggest that Leptocleidus moved into freshwater systems to escape larger plesiosaurs and pliosaurs.
The genus Leptocleidus was first described by Andrews in 1922.
Leptocleidus belongs to the family Leptocleididae.
Leptocleidus is classified within the order Plesiosauria.
The type species of the genus Leptocleidus is L. superstes.
Leptocleidus lived during the Cretaceous period in what is now England, Australia, and South Africa.
Leptocleidus lived between 143.1 and 100.5 million years ago, from the Berriasian to the Albian stages.
The species L. capensis lived during the upper Valanginian age in the Cape Province of South Africa.
L. clemai inhabited the Carnarvon Basin in Western Australia during the Hauterivian-Barremian ages.
L. superstes is known from the Upper Weald Clay in Sussex, England, dating to the Barremian age.
